pr_title: [Core][Distributed] use absolute path for library file
pr_body:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/4155 adds integrity check for nccl library by `ldd`, which causes problem for rocm: `ldd` requires full path of library. Therefore, we need to find full path of the library.

Should fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/4257 .
pr_comments: Tested in AMD machine, `find_library("librccl.so.1") == '/opt/rocm-5.5.1/lib/librccl.so.1'` . I think this PR is good to go now.

This issue also happens on ROCm with the latest 0.4.1 docker built from source. 
I was able to work around it by setting `VLLM_NCCL_SO_PATH=/opt/rocm/lib/librccl.so.1` as recommended in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/4224, so I assume the same can be done for the CUDA equivalent library.

I download and upload the nccl install package from the official website [https://developer.nvidia.com/nccl/nccl-legacy-downloads](https://developer.nvidia.com/nccl/nccl-legacy-downloads).

after then

```
rpm -ivh nccl-local-repo-rhel7-2.16.2-cuda11.8-1.0-1.x86_64.rpm
```

after then in /var/rpm -ivh nccl-local-repo-rhel7-2.16.2-cuda11.8/ and execute the command

```

```
